ownership.load: Core request remains cancellable until completion; success transfers one native full-width resource handle
ownership.close: Core close-handle releases Guest ownership; bindings and frames retain their own references
ownership.prefetch: Cancellable low-priority request; completion releases its cache pin and transfers no handle
ownership.status: Metadata-only package/owner-scoped snapshot; ABSENT=0 QUEUED=1 LOADING=2 READY=3 FAILED=4; does not pin or touch LRU
ownership.read: Cancellable bounded blob read; returns min(requested bytes, total-offset) without block alignment; result bytes are borrowed for the Guest event callback, no handle; offset==total is EOF
ownership.decode-image: Borrowed FILE/STREAM source, revalidated at every read. Core request identity guards cancellation and token reuse. Result handle transfers only on successful completion; no decoder handle or finish command.
ownership.next-image-frame: Borrows the current image until completion or cancellation. Success transfers exactly one new immutable IMAGE handle and moves any decoder state to it; old pixels remain independently valid. Final frames and static images have no decoder state. Cancellation before polling does not advance; after publication the result handle owns the state and must be closed even if abandoned. Closing the current state owner or stopping its component reclaims the decoder. Concurrent advances on one image are rejected.

errors: Immediate rejection has no completion; accepted requests reserve exactly one status-prefixed completion, errors have no trailing result payload

images.formats: PXR1 kind=4, RGB565=2 (little-endian words), BGRA8888=7 (straight alpha bytes), BGRA8888_PREMULTIPLIED=8, or PNG_RGB565=10 (PNG payload, prepared as RGB565 since Assets 2.5); ordinary package PNG encoding=6 is prepared as premultiplied BGRA8888 since Assets 2.4
images.preparation: Offline PXR pixels or, since Assets 2.4, catalogued package PNG (RGBA or indexed). Async LOAD/PREFETCH decodes PNG on the asset worker into premultiplied BGRA8888, with the same bounded/coalescing resident cache, cancellation, pixel and temporary budgets. PNG limits: dimensions <=1024, pixels <=65536, encoded bytes <=524288. QUERY describes the original PNG; successful LOAD/PREFETCH returns the native prepared descriptor. Decoding retains no compressed file copy and preserves the catalog/manifest identity.
images.streaming: Optional image-decode feature. DECODE_IMAGE borrows a component-owned FILE(3) or STREAM(2), reading from its current position until EOF. Host reads at most 4096 bytes per poll in 1024-byte stack chunks; WOULD_BLOCK yields. No encoded data passes through Guest memory. Caller keeps source exclusively readable until completion/cancel; the service never closes it. Pending codec state is reclaimed on error/cancel/stop. Success returns an immutable IMAGE handle with independent lifetime. Formats and native/hardware decoder choice belong to optional Host adapters, not this ABI.
images.frames: Optional image-frames feature. Decode options PNG=1 JPEG=2 GIF=4 (zero accepts any supported format) filter the signature before codec allocation. WITH_FRAMES=256 extends the request from 24 to 32 bytes and result from 36 to 48 bytes. Unknown bits or lengths are invalid. Animation ceilings are zero for ordinary limits, otherwise clamped to ordinary ceilings only for sequence codecs; they do not reduce PNG/JPEG quality. NEXT_IMAGE_FRAME returns the same 48-byte result, flags LAST=1 (all other bits reserved zero). Static images yield one LAST frame. Delays are unsigned milliseconds, iterations start at zero. No timer, automatic decoding or queue is created. NEXT on an image without state is BAD_STATE. An extra resource slot is needed while old and new immutable images coexist.

prepared_rgb565_png: Since Assets 2.5: image encoding 10 is a PXR1 header plus PNG payload. Width/height describe the PNG and decoded-bytes is width*height*2. Limits: dimensions <=1024, pixels <=131072, PNG payload <=524288 bytes. LOAD/PREFETCH decodes directly into RGB565 using the shared cache/pixel budget; no full BGRA intermediate exists. Any non-opaque pixel rejects the load. QUERY describes the stored encoding; successful LOAD/PREFETCH describes prepared RGB565 pixels. Raw PXR encodings and ordinary alpha PNG remain unchanged.
